newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Former Philippine president Macapagal dies at 86.
newsitem.headline: Former Philippine president Macapagal dies at 86.

text.p: Former Philippine president Diosdado Macapagal, who lost his reelection bid to Ferdinand Marcos some 30 years ago, died of illness in a Manila hospital on Monday evening. He was 86.
His doctor, Gary Lopez, said on Tuesday that Macapagal suffered from heart failure, acute kidney failure and pneumonia. He went into hospital on Monday morning.
Macapagal served as the Philippine president from 1961 to 1965. He was defeated during his reelection bid by the late president Marcos, who ruled the country for the next 20 years.
Macapagal served as vice president in 1957 to 1960, after serving two terms as congressman.
In 1962, his government laid formal claim to the then British-held North Borneo territory, which later became part of what is now Malaysia.
Incumbent president Fidel Ramos has shelved the claim, saying the territorial dispute should not impede regional cooperation.

Macapagal was also responsible for changing the date of Philippine independence day to June 12, when revolutionaries declared their independence from Spanish rule at the turn of the century, instead of July 4 when the United States declared Philippine independent after World War Two.
He was one of the political luminaries who supported the ouster of president Marcos in the mid-1980s.
One of his children is Senator Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, who is widely tipped as a possible presidential candidate in the 1998 elections.
